title: Work-Rate and Average-Cost Models
short: Model shared work and average cost with rational equations.
trouble: Students add the times of two workers instead of adding their rates.

blocks.html: Two kinds of real problems lead straight to rational equations: people (or machines) sharing a job, and costs spread over many items.

Work rate: if a job takes $a$ hours, the rate is $\frac{1}{a}$ job per hour, and rates working together add: $\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{t}$. Average cost: with fixed cost $F$ and cost $c$ per item, $\bar{C}(x) = \frac{F + cx}{x}$; set it equal to a target and solve.

Rates add because the amounts of work done in one hour add: if one painter does $\frac{1}{3}$ of the fence each hour and the other does $\frac{1}{6}$, together they do $\frac{1}{2}$ of the fence per hour, so they need 2 hours. Times don't add: two people can't take longer than either one alone. For average cost, the fixed cost is shared by more items as $x$ grows, so $\bar{C}(x) = \frac{F}{x} + c$ gets close to $c$ but never reaches it.

blocks.cap: Average cost $f(x) = \frac{500 + 3x}{x}$ dollars per book. The dashed line $g$ at \$3 is the per-book cost the average approaches. Drag along the curve.

blocks.title: Working together
blocks.q: Ana paints a fence in 3 hours; Ben takes 6 hours. How long together?

blocks.title: Finding one worker's time
blocks.q: Two pumps empty a tank in 4 hours together. The first alone takes 6 hours. How long does the second take alone?

blocks.title: Average cost
blocks.q: Printing costs \$500 to set up plus \$3 per book. How many books make the average cost \$5?

blocks.html: Adding the times. If Ana takes 3 hours and Ben takes 6, "9 hours together" can't be right; together they must be faster than Ana alone. Add the rates $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}$, then flip. Check: in 2 hours Ana paints $\frac{2}{3}$ and Ben paints $\frac{1}{3}$, one whole fence.
